# Astronomy & Cosmology Analysis Guide

Curated by Skill Harbor — a methodical playbook for analyzing astronomical observations and cosmological models with your Muse: framing the question (object type, band, physical quantity), acquiring data from the right archives (Gaia, SDSS, 2MASS/WISE, Chandra, NED, SIMBAD), calibrating and reducing it (bias, flat-fielding, photometry, spectroscopy), deriving physical parameters (distances, masses, compositions), fitting models (stellar atmospheres, N-body, LCDM/wCDM with MCMC), running the cosmological calculations, and visualizing the results — closed by a quality checklist (coordinate epoch, distance method, H0/Omega_m stated, error propagation, selection biases). Discovered via skills.sh, listed here with credit to its creator by @beita6969. Honest caveats: a methodology/knowledge skill — it guides the agent's reasoning rather than executing code; the data itself comes from public archives you query yourself; 25 installs on the catalog, but popularity is not a review. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
